title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Consumer Rights and Responsibilities
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In civic and economic terms, who is formally defined as a **Consumer**?
options: The manufacturer who operates heavy machinery in a factory
An individual who purchases and uses goods and services to satisfy personal or household needs
The government agency responsible for collecting taxes
A wholesale trader who exports local raw materials
questions.explain: A **Consumer** is the end-user in the economic chain; any individual who buys and consumes goods and services to satisfy their personal or family basic needs.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A consumer buys a carton of milk and notices that the manufacturer intentionally scraped off the expiry date and chemical ingredients. Which fundamental consumer right is directly violated here?
options: Right to Redress
Right to Information
Right to Representation
Right to a Healthy Environment
questions.explain: The **Right to Information** entitles consumers to receive full, transparent details about a product, including manufacturing dates, expiry dates, and ingredients, allowing them to make informed choices.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: When a consumer inadvertently purchases a highly defective mobile phone and returns it to the company to lawfully demand a refund, free repair, or replacement, they are actively exercising their Universal Right to:
options: Safety
Redress
Satisfaction of basic needs
Consumer Education
questions.explain: The **Right to Redress** guarantees consumers fair settlement of legitimate claims, meaning they are entitled to compensation, refunds, or replacements for misrepresentation or shoddy, defective goods.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: According to the universal responsibilities of a consumer, what critical action must a consumer take immediately after completing a major transaction to protect themselves in case of a future dispute?
options: Secretly dispose of the purchased product
Demand and carefully keep proofs of transaction, such as receipts, invoices, or warranties
Physically fight the cashier to prove dominance
Immediately resell the item at double the market price
questions.explain: A key **responsibility** of a consumer is to **demand and retain transaction proofs (receipts/warranties)**. This documentation is completely vital if the consumer later needs to seek legal redress for faulty products.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The **Right to Safety** is a heavily enforced universal consumer right. What does it guarantee?
options: Protection against the marketing of goods and services that are hazardous to health, life, or property
That the police will permanently assign an armed guard to every shopper
That a consumer can violently assault shop owners they suspect of cheating
That goods will absolutely never spoil over a 100-year period
questions.explain: The **Right to Safety** strictly protects consumers against the production, marketing, and sale of products (like expired drugs or faulty electronics) that pose a danger to their health or physical property.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: If an industrial manufacturing plant illegally continuously dumps toxic chemical waste into a river that supplies drinking water to a nearby community, which specific universal consumer right is being violently breached?
options: Right to Information
Right to Representation
Right to a Healthy Environment
Right to Redress
questions.explain: The **Right to a Healthy Environment** asserts that consumers have the fundamental right to live and work in an environment that is non-threatening to their well-being, which means freedom from pollution and toxic hazards.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Consumers are formally advised by civic agencies to always 'Think independently'. What does this specific consumer responsibility fundamentally mean?
options: To only buy products that have absolutely zero advertising
To blindly purchase every product endorsed by a popular celebrity
To completely ignore all government safety warnings on packages
To rationally analyze their true needs and avoid being swayed strictly by deceptive or manipulative advertisements
questions.explain: **Thinking independently** implies taking responsibility for one's choices. It requires the consumer to critically evaluate product claims, ignore manipulative advertising, and purchase based on genuine needs and rational budget constraints.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: To guarantee that corporate cheating does not continue, consumers are expected to proactively report fraudulent market practices and unsafe goods to agencies like the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC). This perfectly describes the consumer responsibility to:
options: Respect the environment
Speak out
Maintain silence
Demand discounts
questions.explain: The responsibility to **Speak Out** obligates consumers to report unfair practices, fake products, and grievances to appropriate authorities to protect themselves and other oblivious citizens.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following rights aims to ensure that consumers acquire the necessary knowledge and skills to make confident, informed choices about goods and services throughout their lives?
options: Right to Satisfaction of basic needs
Right to Redress
Right to Consumer Education
Right to Representation
questions.explain: The **Right to Consumer Education** ensures the public is continuously educated about their rights, market trends, and ways to avoid exploitation, empowering them for lifelong economic survival.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Respecting the environment is a core consumer responsibility. Which action directly violates this specific responsibility?
options: Demanding a written invoice after purchasing a refrigerator
Littering nylon packaging on the highway and casually dumping non-biodegradable waste in gutters
Speaking out boldly against fake drugs in the local pharmacy
Seeking consumer education on how to operate heavy machinery
questions.explain: Consumers have a civic duty to **Respect the Environment**. Improperly disposing of product waste (like littering nylon or plastics) severely damages the ecosystem and violates this fundamental responsibility.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A consumer purchases a generator and is handed a written **warranty**. Why is it the strict responsibility of the consumer to demand and safely keep this warranty document?
options: To use it as a substitute for national currency in future purchases
Because it acts as vital legal proof of the transaction, necessary for seeking free repairs, replacement, or redress if the item malfunctions
To prove to their neighbors that they possess expensive electronics
To sell the document to environmental activists
questions.explain: Retaining receipts and **warranties** fulfills the consumer's responsibility to keep transaction proofs. These documents are legally required when a consumer returns to a store to demand their **Right to Redress** for defective goods.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: According to universal consumer standards, the **"Right to Representation to be heard"** implies that consumers are constitutionally entitled to:
options: Have their interests represented, heard, and strongly considered by the government during the formulation of economic and consumer policies
Be granted completely free access to all live music concerts
Speak directly to the President of the country daily regarding minor personal complaints
Be constantly protected by armed military escorts while shopping in local markets
questions.explain: The **Right to Representation (to be heard)** means consumers must have a voice. Their collective interests and grievances must receive due consideration when the government or corporate boards make policies that affect the market.
